summary: Design around people's actual communication, mobility and daily-life needs, including setup and support burdens.
outcomes: Convert stakeholder needs into observable usability requirements.
Evaluate setup, fatigue, error recovery, caregiver burden and accessibility.
sequence: Begin with varied user goals and preferences
Map people, environments and support roles
Evaluate real task completion and workload
Plan ongoing support and co-design feedback

visual.question: What prevents a technically accurate system from being useful at home?
visual.interaction: Explore fictional user scenarios with different motor, sensory and support constraints.

practice.task: Review an interface prototype against two contrasting use scenarios.
practice.success: Produces testable requirements and avoids assuming one person's preferences represent everyone.
